item.title: 1. A business signal
item.description:
The following handoff sets the scene for your investigation:

Finance: We have flagged a gap between completed order value and collected payments. Please investigate the discrepancy and identify which orders are affected.

Operations: We checked the same period. Checkout requests are completing without an increase in errors or latency.

A request can complete successfully while producing the wrong business outcome. Normal request-health signals are useful context, but they do not explain Finance’s discrepancy.

item.title: 2. Scope the investigation
item.description:
Start with a clear scope so that every comparison refers to the same application and period.

Exercise · Open Logs and select your environment
  1. Open Logs from the main navigation in Splunk Observability Cloud. Use Builder for this exercise.
  2. Select the connection and index provided by your instructor.
  3. In the time picker, select Custom → Absolute and enter the investigation window provided by your instructor. Check the displayed timezone, then select Apply. Keep this window unchanged while comparing results.
  4. Remove any trace ID, severity, or other filters left over from an earlier investigation.
  5. Select Add Filter → Fields, search for deployment.environment, select the field, enter your workshop environment, and select include. Repeat for service.name = checkout.
  6. Select Run search.

The timeline summarizes matching log activity. The Logs table contains individual events, and the Fields list helps you explore their structured attributes.

item.title: 3. Find the business event
item.description:
Checkout emits several messages while processing a purchase. Use its order placed event to focus on completed purchases, then inspect the fields you will use to compare each order’s value with its charge.

Exercise · Inspect the order’s business fields
  1. Keep the search scope and investigation window from Step 2.
  2. Select Add Filter → Keyword, enter order placed, and select include. Select Run search.
  3. Open a row in the Logs table and confirm that the message field in its JSON body is order placed.

These completion events give you a consistent set of purchases to investigate.

item.title: 4. Find and explain the discrepancy
item.description:
Use the completed-order search from Step 3. You will add columns to the Logs table so each row shows an order’s value, charge, and eventually the reason for the difference.

Keep the same connection, index, environment, checkout service, order placed event, and investigation window. Retain any required USD currency filter. Keep all completed orders in the results; adding columns changes the table display without changing your search.

Exercise · Show the order value and amount charged

  1. Select the Configure Table gear above the Logs table to open Table Settings. Deselect _raw to make room for the business fields; Severity and Time remain visible.

item.title: 5. Save the search and verify results
item.description:
Save a search so you can return to this investigation and check new orders after a fix. In this workshop, there are no legitimate free orders, so a positive-value completed purchase with a zero charge warrants investigation.

Exercise · Save the investigation
  1. Retain your connection, index, environment, checkout service, and order placed event. Remove any order ID, trace ID, pod, or promo-code restriction used to inspect an individual case.
  2. Open an affected order and select the 0 value for app.order.amount.charged.usd. Select More (⋯) → Add to filter, then run the search to narrow the results to zero-charge orders.
  3. Inspect a matching order and confirm that app.order.amount.usd is positive. The saved search finds zero charges; a responder uses the event details to verify the order’s full value.
  4. Select Save as → Save query. Enter a unique name such as <your-name> — zero-charge orders.

Add a short description, review the query’s scope, and leave public sharing off unless your instructor asks you to share it. Select Save, then find the query in Saved Queries. Reapply the intended investigation window when reopening it.
